utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me say at the outset that in the absence of Judge Van den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Mr. Groome, you may not have understood me yesterday when I asked you to confirm when was the first time five sets of documents were disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence, because it may be that I wasn't sufficiently clear. I identified five witnesses and I want to find out when was the first time that these documents were disclosed to the Defence. VG-094, two documents; Wil Fagel, 10 documents; VG-042, five documents; VG-131, ten documents; and VG-138, 1 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first time that they were disclosed, with exceptions that are listed in the annex, was the date of that disclosure. So if you look in the last column in the annex, some of those documents with respect to one of the witnesses, and I forget precisely which one, it says previously disclosed by e-mail and it gives the date. I believe I have a copy of the filing from yesterday, Your Honour. If I can ... So, Your Honour, with respect to VG-042, if you look in the far right column, item 16 was disclosed on 22nd of September, 2008, and item number 17 was disclosed by e-mail on the 22nd of October, 2008. Then the other materials, Your Honour, this was the first disclosure on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Groome. Thanks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on a related topic that Your Honour had also asked for information about disclosures in September. I have two attorneys working on that, and by tomorrow we will be making a written submission that in great detail sets out all of the history of the disclosure of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So we are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next witness for the Prosecution that the Prosecution will call, Your Honour, would be Mr. Ib Jul Hansen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let Mr. Hansen be called, subject to what Mr. Cepic has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, yesterday during the examination by my omission I forgot to request admission of document ICRC list of missing person in Visegrad. I used that document in the cross-examination of witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 2D26, Your Honours. MR.IVETIC: And, Your Honours, I would just take the opportunity to bring to the Court's attention, I believe courtesy copies were served of our motion relating to the testimony of Mr. Masovic, who is scheduled to be the second witness today, and it's a very -- we believe very serious matter that goes to the integrity of his evidence and the proceedings and what ought to be properly brought in through that witness. We would bring that to Your Honours' attention so that if you don't have a copy if that could be provided to you so that you have time to review the same, and if need be, ask for additional information in oral submissions which we would be more than happy to provide following Mr. Hansen's testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I can see I am going to have a problem with the way you speak. I have difficulty understanding you perhaps because you speak very fast. You are saying that a motion has been filed, is that it? MR.IVETIC: That's correct, Your Honours. A motion has been filed clarifying our objections to Mr. Masovic's testimony and, in particular, aspects of his written statement and where they are actually asking Mr. Masovic to do what Your Honours told us in the last week in this courtroom that we cannot do which is to present testimony of witnesses who are out-of-court declarants by way of written statement by presenting to a witness who is not the out-of-court declarant. The statement of Mr. Masovic is about two-thirds full of conclusions that Mr. Masovic reaches and presents based upon statements that we neither have disclosed to us nor have been opportunity to investigate or confront relating to out of court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let us deal with that when the time comes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: MR.IVETIC: Fair enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness read the declaration. Please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. You may begin, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, can I ask you to begin by stating your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: My name is Ib Jul Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I was born in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly observe the pause between questions and answers for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are both being asked to observe a pause between question and answer in the interest of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the town Randers in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when were you born?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I was born on the 31st of December, 1944.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You were an employee of the ICTY, the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you, in a sentence or two, to summarize your investigative experience prior to coming to work at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I joined the Danish police back in 1969 and since 1974 I've been employed with criminal investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you first come to the Office of the Prosecutor at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I was seconded from my government from 1995 to 1997, and then in 1999, I joined the Tribunal as a staff member, investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you terminate your employment?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I terminated my employment at the end of 2006 when I turned 62 years, which is the maximum age for an -- sorry, for an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you currently engaged in any work for your government?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I am. When I returned to my country, I joined the reserve police, and I'm now part-time employed with the Danish police reserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what unit do you currently work in?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I work in a unit called Special International Crimes Office, which is located in Copenhagen. And this unit is dealing with crimes committed abroad by persons that are living in our country.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I know that you worked on several investigations for the Office of the Prosecutor. Was the investigation into events in Visegrad one of them?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you work on that investigation?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I believe I worked from the very beginning of 2000 until sometime in 2003, maybe a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you have a primary partner or colleague that you worked with on this investigation?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. My partner in the investigation was Canadian investigator Yves Roy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to summarize your responsibilities on the case?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We tried to find witnesses in the former Yugoslavia or abroad concerning incidents that happened in Visegrad in 1992, and we interviewed those witnesses. We also collected evidence and we did a few searches, and, yeah, that's more or less what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you list some of the names of the people whose activities you were investigating in relation to crimes committed in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Shortly before my arrival, an indictment was created including three persons, Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic. And we concentrated on investigating those three persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time you began your investigation, did you know what Milan Lukic looked like?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know what Sredoje Lukic looked like?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly observe the pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Apologies to the Interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were able to obtain a confirmed photo image of Mr. Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I believe in June 2000, my colleague Yves Roy came across a videotape in Sarajevo showing Milan Lukic attending a wedding in Visegrad a few years before, most probably 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were able to obtain an image of Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. By coincidence during the Mitar Vasiljevic case, after the arrest of Mitar Vasiljevic, we were looking through a lot of videotapes from 1992, 1993 shot in Visegrad, and one of those sequences that were in the hands of the Tribunal already in 1998 showed an incident that took place at the very beginning of a war at a dam outside Visegrad where, I don't know how many, a handful of police officers maybe were held hostages by a Muslim, he was called an extremist, and after some days they were released. After the release of the police officers, they gave interviews to the press, and one of those interviews were in one of the numerous videotapes that we had from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the course of your duties on the Visegrad investigation, or in particular, this case, were you called upon to try to identify the whereabouts of both Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you conducted photo identification procedures in relation to this case? When I say "this case," I mean the original indictment of all three men, Mr. Vasiljevic and the two Lukics?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. We went through all statements that were taken and found possible -- found persons that might be able to recognise the suspects. And we decided to go and see those persons and ask them to pick photos in a photo array that were arranged by a staff member Zoran Lecic here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The photo -- the initial photospread, how many photographs in total did it include?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The initial photospread included ten photos. Later on we created a new one including 12 photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there any photographs of the three men the subject of the indictment placed in that -- in those original photo arrays?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. We used the arrest photo of Mitar Vasiljevic, and then we had some concern concerning the photos that we froze from the videotapes because they didn't fit in the -- they didn't look like the arranged photos that were put on the original photospread with Milan -- sorry, Mitar Vasiljevic photo. So we had some problems. We decided to show a photospread for most of the witnesses including only Mitar Vasiljevic who was arrested already at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The photographs of the other people in the photospread, where did you obtain those from?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Zoran Lecic got them from the Dutch authorities, and we asked for persons that had a Balkan look, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that Prosecution Exhibit 87 be now displayed on the monitor. Mr. Hansen, the monitor to your right will in a few minutes show a document. When it does appear, I would ask you whether you recognise it. While we are waiting for that document to load, can I ask you a question with respect to the photo array. In which position in the photo array was Mitar Vasiljevic placed?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: He was placed in different positions. So we shuffled the photos so he wasn't on each A4-size paper not in the same position. So once he was, let's say, number 3, the next that was shown he was number 4 and number 11, and so in order to avoid problems that could arise when witnesses met and talked about this, so they shouldn't be able to tell that Mitar or the suspect was number 3 in the top row.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you see P87 now before you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We are looking at an array with 12 persons, one of whom is Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When a witness was shown such a photo array, how were the results recorded?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We interviewed the witness -- or I, to speak for myself, I interviewed the witness. I wrote a statement, and the comments from the witness were stated in that statement. And at the end, the witness signed the photospread and also had the statement read back and signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what question was put to the witness when they were shown the photospread?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: First of all, if they recognised any on the photospread. And if they said yes, I ask who, and then they pointed to the person that they thought they knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were these photo arrays ever used with groups of witnesses or more than one witness at a time?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, no, no. It was always one witness at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, did you personally conduct some photo identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I think I conducted ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to be asking the witness about specific information I think too much to retain in his memory. He has made some notes and he has brought some of his records from that time and some of the statements. I would ask that, with permission of Court, when necessary he be allowed to refer to some of these notes to refresh his recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where were the notes made?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The notes were made in his review of his statements earlier this week, Your Honour. So I'm about to ask him which ten people he showed a photo array to. He has gone through all of the records and he has made a list to refresh his memory about the ten witnesses who he showed photo arrays to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And all of that was done, you say, earlier this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, the statements, Your Honour, as we've heard him say, he recorded the results in the statements. Now he has made some notes to cross-reference the statements to assist him in remembering. He is going to be talking about several dozen witnesses and who did -- showed what photo arrays to which witness. It's not something that he was able to keep in his mind or in his memory and is asking for an opportunity to refresh his memory when necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just -- we simply have not -- we would like a copy of the notes if the Court -- otherwise we would object. But if the Court allows it from a refreshing recollection perspective, I understand this witness did deal with a voluminous amount of documents and witnesses, we would like a copy of the witness's notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm disposed to allow it. Do you have a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't have a copyright now, Your Honour. I can either have someone run out and make a copy now or I can have it done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen appears to have one. Do you have an --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The notes are handwritten, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, how long would it take?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The usher is telling us that we may be able to make a copy in hopefully a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. The usher will see to the copying of this statement. We have very advanced technology here. It works most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might seem a bit out of order, but while we are standing here might I make -- raise an issue with the Chamber and make productive use of this hiatus? It's nothing related to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, as long as it's appropriate to raise it in the witness's presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the beginning of the week you asked for written submissions on in-court identifications and related questions and the deadline given was Friday. The submission is well underway and it is our present intention to file it late Friday evening. It occurs to me that, Your Honour, that it will not be distributed by the registry until Monday morning. Given the importance of the issue, and the fact that the document would benefit from the extra two days of work over the weekend, would the Chamber consider extending the deadline to 9.30 on Monday morning with the provision that the parties also send courtesy copies to the senior legal officer, and that way, I believe the Chamber would have hopefully an improved submission at the same time it would have had the submission were it filed Friday evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And the submissions from the Defence, Mr. Alarid and Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, we were working on ours. Marie was working on it last night until late. We were intending to do it late tomorrow night as well, so we would have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll grant the extension requested by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the same will apply for the Defence, if they wish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, perhaps there's some other areas that I can move on to that may not require the kind of detailed memorization such as witness's pseudonyms. Were any photo arrays containing a photograph of Sredoje Lukic ever shown to a witness?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No. We decided not to show any photo of Sredoje Lukic because of the quality of the -- it wasn't an original tape but we will call it the original tape. It was very poor quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was your concern given the quality of the photograph of him?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We thought it might be possible for the witness to pick that picture without knowing or -- because of the quality, it would be easy for a witness to see that this wasn't an original photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And with that --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. At the same time, this poor quality photo was used on the SFOR posters that were put up all over Bosnia after the indictment was, how do you call it, unsealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For those of us who might not be familiar with the SFOR posters, can I ask you to describe in essence what the SFOR posters were that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The posters were pictures of the fugitives with their names and day of birth and put up on official offices in -- all over Bosnia and Herzegovina and other former Yugoslavian republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your concern about showing a photo array that had a picture from the SFOR poster?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Because SFOR poster was known by each and everybody, each and everyone in the former Yugoslavia, that's what we believed, and in order to avoid any problems by identification, we decided not to show the photo from the poster in the photo array.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the photograph of Milan Lukic placed in any photo array that was shown to a witness?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was placed in one photo array that I showed to a person who was in a country far from the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why was -- why was it different rationale applied in this case?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We thought it was acceptable because the location of this country, this witness didn't have the opportunity to see the posters that were in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there -- do you recall the pseudonym of this witness, or do you need your notes to --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I believe it's VG-032.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know with respect to which crime in the indictment he was a witness?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: He was a witness in the -- what we called the Drina killings, an incident took place north of Visegrad at the Drina bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the photo array that was shown to him, were there any photographs of other people listed on the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. There was a photo of Mitar Vasiljevic. And I remember the witness pointed the photo of Mitar Vasiljevic 100 per cent sure, but then he commented on the photo of Milan Lukic saying that he was 90 percent sure of this was Milan Lukic. He further said that he had, I don't remember whether he had lost weight or gained weight, and he looked older than he remembered him. Because he picked him with only 90 percent, he decided not to sign the photo array.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was his statement about being 90 percent sure recorded in his statement which he then signed?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We are still waiting for your notes to return. Trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm told that they should be here shortly. Let me just get it clear, this photo array was shown to the witnesses the last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was it shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: These were -- perhaps I better ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The photo arrays were shown from mid-2000 until mid-2001, approximately. I showed them during this period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When were the accused arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the summer of 2005, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During your time working on the case, did you ever come into possession of photographs of either Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic that you thought could appropriately be used in a photospread?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I remember once we was on a mission to Belgrade. I don't remember when it was, maybe 2003 or 2004. I had problem with the witness that didn't show up, so instead of just sitting, waiting and doing nothing, I decided together with an interpreter to go and see the newly established Serbian war crimes unit, a courtesy visit. And I was well received. We discussed certain cases, and I asked, Do you by the way have fingerprints or a photo of Milan Lukic. And he said, the leader of the unit, Yes, we have, just request them. So when I came home we requested those photos and they were used for the red notice with Interpol later on. I was told the photos -- the photo was taken when Milan Lukic was arrested for, as far as I remember, illegal weapon possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you ever hold identification parades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. You are not familiar with the practice of an identification parade in which an accused is put in a parade with a number of other men and a witness asked to identify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have to -- I have to say that at the end of 2004, I left The Hague for -- and spent my last two service years in Sarajevo. So I left the investigations here and did something else at the Sarajevo field office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is taking much longer now than I thought it would. Far too long. It's not a profitable use of the Court's time. Can you proceed until such time as we have the copies of the notes. And it's only because Mr. Alarid said he wanted it and I believe he would be entitled to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Hopefully they are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, can I now ask you, returning to where we were before we attempted to photocopy your notes, how many witnesses did you personally conduct a photo identification procedure with?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: For this purpose I met with ten witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to slowly just enumerate them so we have them on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to summarize the results. It's not directly relevant to this case, but if you just summarize the results.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. VG-003 said or picked Mitar Vasiljevic. VG-024 picked Mitar Vasiljevic. VG-032 picked Mitar Vasiljevic and said he was always with Milan Lukic. VG-059 picked Mitar Vasiljevic. VG-060 picked not with 100 percent Mitar Vasiljevic. VG-064 picked Mitar Vasiljevic, and so did VG-078. VG-089 said he or she knew the face but didn't remember the name. VG-104, that's something special because it was a photo array with a person in by the name Momir Safic and this Momir Safic was picked. And VG-101, Mitar was picked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to the photo identifications that you personally conducted, are all of the photo arrays accounted for and available should the Chamber wish to look at them?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, unfortunately, the photo array for VG-003 is not available.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from that one, are the other ones accounted for and available?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you briefly about whether you are aware of photospreads done by other investigators?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. In total five investigators did this during the investigation. Besides me, it's Yves Roy. It's investigator Rita Pradhan and investigator Azela Dassanayake and investigator Finn Tollefson.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you ask you to deal with Yves Roy first. How many photo identification procedures did he perform?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yves Roy performed six.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you enumerate the witnesses that he conducted such procedures with.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, he -- Witness VG-038 picked Mitar Vasiljevic. VG-058 picked or recognised, as it's written in the statement, Mitar Vasiljevic and added he is always with Mitar Lukic [sic]. VG-079 picked Mitar Vasiljevic. VG-084 didn't pick any. VG-097 picked Mitar Vasiljevic and the last one was [indiscernible] who also picked --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Picked who, sorry?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we now deal with Rita Pradhan, how many did she conduct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: She conducted two. VG-013, and the witness picked Mitar Vasiljevic. And VG-63 was negative. The witness didn't pick anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So to be clear, when you say "negative," when asked did you recognise anyone, the witness said, I do not?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Finn Tollefson?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Finn Tollefson met with one witness, VG-119. 119. And she said or I don't know -- I think it was a woman, mentioned that she had seen number 7 and number 4 before but she didn't give a name, and number 4 was the photo of Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then finally, investigator Dassanayake, you mentioned that that investigator also showed some photographs. Were these the photo arrays that you've been describing?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No. Azela Dassanayake met with three witnesses back in 1998, and those photos that he showed the witness -- showed for the witnesses were surveillance photos taken in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who were the surveillance photos taken by?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: They were taken by SFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the purpose of these surveillance photos?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: To identify whether -- try and identify whether Milan Lukic was in Visegrad at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to ask that ERN number 06428898-06428903 be shown. Your Honour, just to note, this is not something that is on the 65 ter list. I'm not seeking to admit it. This is one of the collections of photos that was found quite recently. It is not a photograph of Milan Lukic, but I believe it would be important for the witness to describe what occurred when this witness -- when he showed these photographs -- or when these photographs were shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness this: In relation to all of the witnesses, you use the word "picked." But in one case, you said a witness "recognised."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a distinction and what is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if there's a difference, but I'm using the word that was in the statement taken by Yves Roy when he met with the witness. He said "recognised." I'm a little reluctant about the meaning of that word, that's why I used the word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you are just simply using the word that the witness used in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While these photographs are being brought up, who are these photographs shown to?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The photos were shown to VG-014, VG-024 and VG-025.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of showing these photographs to these witnesses?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The purpose was to establish whether Milan Lukic was one of the persons on the photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why did SFOR want to have that information or why were -- what was the purpose?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: They wanted to arrest him, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it a picture of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was never established whether it was Milan Lukic or somebody that looked like him. The witnesses that Azela met with had some comments that I don't have in my papers, but were -- the wording were in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's do each witness individually. And first, what period of time were witnesses shown these photographs?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It happened in December 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who is the first witness that was shown?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: VG-014 said that there was some similarity to Milan Lukic, but since the photos were vague, he or she wouldn't say anything for sure. Witness VG-024 said that the person in the red jacket was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: And Witness VG-025 said that the photos resembled Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I would like to reserve the ability to recall this witness understanding on the Defence case that he was one of the obvious primary investigators in this case. However, today we'll just be touching on the identification issues raised on direct by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are saying you'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, we may call him in the Defence case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the Defence case, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. But given the limited direct examination, we are just going to touch on the issues as given. Could the court assistant go back to the photospread including Mitar Vasiljevic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And good afternoon, Inspector Hansen. Are you still -- you are still currently a police officer; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes and no. I'm a reservist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: My name is Jason Alarid and I represent Milan Lukic. And just going to this, this photo array, is it -- just a second. The photo array that included Mitar Vasiljevic as is, you used the same -- and you said Dutch photographs, they were from Dutch authorities?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: They are from Dutch police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you did have some relationship with the Balkan authorities. Why not use photographs, mug shots, whatnot, from the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We didn't or the investigations team didn't request those photos. We just requested and array, and later on, I was told by Zoran Lecic that he got them from the Dutch police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did I hear you correctly that one point in time Momir Safic was included in this photo array?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at one time was Sredoje Lukic included in this photo array?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we simply mark this as a Defence exhibit and have it introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's already in evidence as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Oh, is it? In relation to which witness was it entered under?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It's P87, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you'll have 45 minutes for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Exhibit was admitted with the Witness VG-078.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could next we call up 1D21-0316.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is this the photograph you recovered from the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I have a smaller version, this is what we received in terms of being blown up, but we just kept it as part of the packet. And can we just quickly go through the next two pages of this exhibit. And this is the fingerprint board you received?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Milan Lukic name is on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise it? Did you handle this document at some point in your career?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No. I never handled that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was sent to the request unit from the Serbian authorities and from there it went to Interpol.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But it did come with the same packet with the aforementioned photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Next page, please. And again, is this a continuation of that, a palm print?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Well, it's a palm print, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And just looking at the ERN numbers, does it appear to be part of the same packet you received for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I didn't receive the package for Milan Lukic. It was requested from ICTY's request unit and it was sent to the request unit from the Serbian authorities. Later on, we received copies of this in the team area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And next page, please. And does this appear to be the internal memorandum related to that ICTY request unit?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It seems so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is that on the regular and customary format that the request unit would use?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And next page, please. And this is a translation we received in relation to the response of the liaison in Belgrade, and does this appear to be the letter that accompanied the said documents?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And next page. And this appears to be the official Yugoslav document and I won't ask you to read that one, of course.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point in time we would ask that 1D21-0316 be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think clearly Mr. Hansen recognised the photograph. I'm very reluctant to agree to or not object to the admission of fingerprints. Clearly Mr. Hansen isn't able to say that they are the fingerprints. I see ERN numbers on it. It may be a matter, and I'm happy to work with Mr. Alarid on this, if I can confirm that this is -- this is in fact something that we did receive. I will stipulate or I will agree to the admission of them, but at this point I'd have to object until I have an opportunity to check with the request unit to see if this was, in fact, something that was transmitted to our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, of course we received them from the Office of the Prosecutor so we just assumed, and they are batched in consecutive ERN numbers, so we just assumed they are all together and contemporaneous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So until authenticated we can mark them for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objection to them being marked so, Your Honour, and I will try to confirm sometime today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit 1D71, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we then place on 1D21-0301. Sorry, it's 1D0021? I am sorry, 1D21-00301. I apologise, it's 00300. I've got to say, scanning reduces the quality of what we have printed out, Your Honour, considering the nature of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, sir, can you recognise the photographs on this page?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I think the photo in the lower right corner is the one from the poster.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And also on the lower left-hand corner as well?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, looks so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And is that the photo lower left-hand corner minus the miniature photo to the left of it, was that the one that was used with VG-032?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And just to let you know we got these photos off the internet so that's where we pulled them off to do a board. Is it fair to say that the one in the upper right-hand corner stating "2001 Lukic, Milan," you had that in your possession as of 2003?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Is that the one I saw a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe so, just big and ...

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: If that's the case -- if that's the one from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, assuming you had that from 2003, what prevented you from -- because would it be fair to say given the nature of the photoboards that you produced earlier, this would have been an appropriate photo sort of in that mug shot array that you used with Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: We decided to stick with the original or with the plans we had from the very start that we wouldn't present witnesses for photos that were not of a decent quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, could the court assistant approach with the ELMO, please, for the use with the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is just what we scanned in, so obviously there is some problems. When you scan something in it tended to darken the photographs and obscure some of the details, but it would be fair to say that the photo as you see on the ELMO in the upper right-hand corner is of better quality, of course, than what we scanned in.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I am assuming that when you received the photo in 2003, it was of a better quality than maybe an ordinary photocopy.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I have to say again, I didn't receive any photos in 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Then let me just ask you, just assuming, since you are an investigator, would the photo as presented on the ELMO be of a sufficient quality to do a photoboard with?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And there's nothing that prevents you as an investigator from going back and re-interviewing witnesses for purposes of clarifying identification; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that there was nothing that prevented you in 2003, even before Mr. Lukic was apprehended, that would have prevented you from approaching all of the witnesses, if you chose, with new photoboards and arrays?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That would be possible, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And of course, we've seen interviews and follow-up interviews in this case that have gone right up to the month before they testified. And is it fair to say that that is an ordinary practice in proofing and following up of an investigation?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: For instance, we had a witness testify yesterday that gave her statement as recently as a month ago before trial.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: So that's a question in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, yeah. So what I'm saying is there's nothing -- the investigation is ongoing until the conviction is done; would that be true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And so there's nothing that prevented the ICTY or the OTP in producing identification boards using, let's say, this photograph at any time prior to trial; would that be true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And there would be nothing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please pause. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were there any discussions following the receipt of the 2003 photograph amongst the investigators working to undertake that role of new photoboards and contacting witnesses?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: There were no discussion among us because actually we didn't know whether we had received this material or not. It happened at a later stage because the material was given to the unit dealing with tracing fugitives, and that was a unit that didn't share the information with the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, just looking at the photograph of Mr. Lukic in uniform, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was the Office of the Prosecutor in possession of that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I've seen it in the team office, yes. Our team area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And in the Balkan theatre, it wasn't uncommon for soldiers to have these kind of photographs taken; would that be true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't know but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what I ask of you is: Were any efforts undertaken to -- because, of course, when you do a photo array, you have to take -- you have to use photographs that are of all a similar nature, such as in Mitar Vasiljevic you used sort of a mugshot approach to the photo array. Simple head shots, nothing in the background, nothing to differentiate where the photos were taken, that kind of thing; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but it's also possible in a photo array to use similar photos so long as they are similar enough, i.e., you could have used several photographs of soldiers in uniform and camouflage, upper body shots, and that would have complied with your requirements for a photo array; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But we could also have decided not to show any photos and just go for the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Correct. Correct. But I mean, identification is an important part of this case; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because these are supposedly eyewitness account and victim accounts of crimes directly perpetrated by my client; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, of course, it's important to exhaust all remedies in your investigation, is it not?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when identification is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly observe pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Again too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. You know when you give me 45 minutes and I have an English speaker, I tend to want to get in as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please pause to ensure an accurate record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You've heard that now. You have been reprimanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So in any identification case, if possible, photo identification or photo lineups should be used; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I think it depends on the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in these circumstances, the OTP was in possession of a useable photograph as early as 2003; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The one I found in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Lukic was arrested when?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I think he was arrested on the 8th of August, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just from a follow-up perspective, there was nothing that prevented your office from revisiting each and every witness with a new photo array; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the investigative team of the Office of the Prosecutor failed to do that; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: If we had the means, I think I would be happy to go and see each and every witness at a later stage, but there was a lot of economic problems and we were not allowed to travel as much as we did before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, have you ever looked at the Interpol warrant that went out?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you aware that the description of Milan Lukic as a blond-haired, blue-eyed individual with tattoos went out over Interpol?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I've never seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that the arrest warrant that led to the arrest of Mr. Lukic in Argentina in Spanish described him as blue eyes, blond hair and with tattoos?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, would it be -- I mean, I understand there were multiple investigators on this team and not all of you touched the same witness personally; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But did the investigators make a concerted effort to coordinate the information that they were gathering and cross-reference the witnesses for possible problems with the case?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. For a long period of time, I would say for most of the time I took part in the investigation I was working closely with Yves Roy and sometimes we were supported by one of the other investigators at the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Not very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you -- do you recall seeing identifying features that disputed what you knew of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I can't remember for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I mean, there's certain instances where some witnesses have him 200 centimetres tall.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You don't?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I'll dig it out eventually. But if I were to tell you that some people described him as very tall --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I know it's a problem describing people because you always have to compare with something. The witnesses that I met I asked always -- if I asked for a description, to compare the person they describe with me, with my height and then put a hair colour on and maybe an eye colour and that's the way -- that's normal police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at this time, Your Honour, just before I forget, I had like to place the 1D210300 into evidence, and I think it might be proper to put the ELMO version in as a hard copy as well simply because it's a better quality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number 1D72, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we bring up ERN number 02008281. And I'd -- can we go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I asked, Your Honour, is this is the photo array for VG -- oh, apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the photo -- now, were there wanted posters for Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, there were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But there are procedures that you can use to ensure that a photo array is relevant with a witness; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, how about this: If you have someone that you want to use a photoboard with, before you show it to them you can simply ask them first how they knew or know the person; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you can ask them if they have ever seen photographs of that person; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's possible, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you can did them if they've looked on the internet, just out of their own curiosity, to see if there's photographs; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I have never asked that question to a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, it's because it's new for, I think, a lot of us as well.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you can also ask them if they watch television, seen any news reports or photographs on the news.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again, would the speakers kindly observe the pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For the hundredth time, please observe a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, it's my understanding that based on the procedure you used, when you interviewed a person, let's say you interviewed them for a few hours, was that about the norm for each witness?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Not always a few hours. Could be four, five, six hours with a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And some witnesses even took multiple days; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at the final meeting of that witness, you had prepared the statement, read it back to them and had them sign it; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's the procedure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in the middle of that statement, between the statements, you probably were doing your work of generating a statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's not my procedure. My procedure was to let the witness talk to the statement and I wrote what he said. We didn't arrange anything, or I didn't arrange anything interviewing a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What do you mean by "arrange"?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I thought you asked whether I arranged the statement during those two or three days when the -- let's say the interview took two or three days, and then I arranged it so it had a -- it looked nice, and so I had a plan from -- I've always had a plan from the beginning which points to go through and then at the end would be shown the witness the photo array.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I guess -- because I don't see memorialized in the statement that question and answer of, Have you seen this person on television, have you seen photographs of them, and I'm assuming in the statement it would say, I have not seen him on TV, I've not seen the photographs, and then I've been shown a photo array including 12 photographs. I didn't see that memorialized in the statements. Is that --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I didn't ask that question. It depended on what the witness told me. We discussed the suspect, of course, and I never asked a direct, sorry, a direct question to the witness concerning his knowledge about, let's say, he read the newspaper or he saw him on television or he heard something from outside --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why wouldn't you ask that direct question?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was all in the indirect discussion with the witness. So it wasn't my -- it wasn't me who put the words in the witness's mouth. It was -- I wrote down what the witness told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But still, isn't it important for an investigator to ferret out whatever issues may complicate the case for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's also what I thought I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But if you are showing photo arrays, wouldn't one of the things to ferret out was simply to ask those direct questions because they don't contaminate the witness's knowledge? They either say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I asked the witness whether they recognised any on this photoboard, this specific photoboard and then I jotted down their answer, and then I asked whom do you recognise and then he or she pointed out that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, I mean, even though it's the picture of Milan Lukic on this, what is on the screen, he is clearly you know looking in a different direction, it's not a straight-ahead shot such as the rest, so I can see why you could say it differentiated a little bit. But regardless of that fact, you still could have attempted to use these photoboards so long as you asked those direct questions; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you chose not to do that; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But in this particular case, why would you choose to do it only with VG-032?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Because he was in a country far from the former Yugoslavia. He didn't have the possibility to watch the posters in which this photo was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, couldn't you have simply asked each witness, Have you seen those photos on the wanted posters?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I could, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if they had said no, you could have whipped out the photoboard and it would have probably been in compliance with the procedure; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: But if they said no, was that right? You never know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you don't know if these witnesses are lying to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: You never know whether a witness is lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You don't know if they might have motives other than telling the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's the main object to interview a witness to get the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in this theatre, issues of revenge definitely is a factor?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't hope so but for some it is, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because someone might point out someone they believe did one thing but they'll point them out for something else because that's the question you asked them.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It's all -- it's not facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, for instance, in the issue of Milan Lukic, the issue of Behija Zukic came up over and over again in your investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Now, I have to remember who is Behija Zukic. Who is Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The owner of the Passat.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And I think you probably got through the witnesses you interviewed that she was a loved figure amongst the people and a well-known figure?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: She was a well-known figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And everyone had a distaste for Milan Lukic because they believed he killed her because they had supposedly see him in her car; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't know if it's correct, but it was said that Milan Lukic killed this woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And yet that is not one of the charges in the indictment; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we introduce this exhibit 02008281 into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D73, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we now call up 1D21-0279.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, while we are waiting for that, sir, isn't it true that when you use a photo array, it's not important that the subject witness knows the alleged perpetrator; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: If the witness doesn't know the perpetrator, there's no reason for using a photo array.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I mean, in light of the Judge's question for a lineup, I mean, let's just use a purse snatching scenario. You think you got the purse snatcher, you get a picture of the purse snatcher, put it in an array, we can assume the witness didn't know the purse snatcher, but you want that witness to see if that's the person they recognise as grabbing their purse and returning away?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Oh, you mean knowing by name?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Not knowing at all. Really, the purpose of a photo array or any kind of lineup is merely identification; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because recognition is separate; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Recognition -- and the reason I did that is, do you recognise what is on the screen, please? And go up a little bit, please, so we see just -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I think it's a page from the ICTY Rules of Procedure and Evidence or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you are obligated to follow these rules when you can; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: All right. Now, just simply read the sentence regarding recognition, please, because isn't it true that investigators must distinguish between recognition and identification?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Okay. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so do you see what I'm saying is that there's no requirement that the person being shown a photoboard having had known the person before from a personal nature; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so regardless of the fact that a lot of the witnesses said they knew Milan Lukic from childhood or earlier, there was nothing that prevented you from showing photoboards to people that both claimed to have never met him before to those people that said they knew him their whole lives?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right, but we decided, as I told before, not to put that photo from the videotape in the photoboard. On this in one -- once we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because -- did you ever consider in your investigation the commonality of the name Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just in terms of things, I mean, you know every ethnicity or nationality has some names that are very common. You know, the classic American is John Smith. There's lots of Smiths. Did you take any consideration in your investigation that Lukic is a common name in Serbia and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't take -- or I didn't take into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you take into consideration that there are several names that are similar, Lukic, Lucic, minor variations in spelling but all around that same sounding name?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What about Milan? Did you take any consideration that Milan is a common name in Serbia and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you take into consideration that there are similarities to even Milan, like Mile, Milos?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, could we please go down to number 2, and the first bullet point, and I'd like you to read that, please.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: "Prepare photoboard of not less than eight photos. Only one photograph of the suspect is to be included. Where there are multiple suspects, separate photoboards must be used for each suspect."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you see "must" or "shall" in a rule book, that is something that is not open to discussion; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, English isn't my first language.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. But in terms of "must," I would assume that that means you should use two photoboards per accused; correct? Excuse me, a photoboard for each accused?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, looks so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so the photoboard that included both Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic would be void pursuant to this bullet point; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the photoboard that you used with Mr. Simsic and Mr. Vasiljevic would have been void for that reason as well.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- I don't know which one you are talking about now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I may have gotten the name wrong. Isn't it true that there was another instance where Mitar Vasiljevic was combined with another accused on a photoboard? I could have heard you --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Can I have a look at my notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The only one it could be would be VG-104.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's, I am sorry, Momir Safic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. And on that board were Mitar and Milan not -- there were no pictures of those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we go to page 2 of what is on the screen, please, "Procedure with the witness." Now, of course once a photoboard has been used with the witness, sir, you are not supposed to use it with another witness in the same sequence; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's why you shuffle photos between witnesses; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, procedure with the witness, could you please read that first paragraph for the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: "The investigator must ascertain whether the witness has seen the suspect in a photograph, on television or on a poster. It may be that the photoboard procedure would then be inappropriate. The team legal advisor should be consulted if an identification (as opposed to recognition) witness has seen the suspect in such circumstances."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you -- could you -- so then wouldn't it be true that every witness that you used the photoboard that you did not ascertain that ahead of time could be null and void?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Let me just read this once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And so do you have an answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Please, your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be true that unless the investigator ascertains whether a witness has seen the suspect in a photograph, on television or poster, it's -- the photo array may be null and void for failure to ask that question?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. According to what is written here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so could we please have 1D21-0297 entered into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And now --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D74, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And now could we have 1D21-0310.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just another 5 minutes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's why I've been hurrying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, this was the surveillance photos shown by the Prosecutor to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But there was two other photos, that's X1. Could we go to the next page, please. Page 3, please. I apologise, and this is X2 as referenced in the identification. That's a little bit closer; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that two witnesses identified this person as Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we please --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure it was 2.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But at least one of, was it VG-025 and VG-024 and VG-014 that all looked at these photos; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that VG-024 and VG-025 identified the gentleman in the red jacket as Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: VG-025 said the picture resembled Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And it was VG-014 who couldn't tell; correct?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we have 1D21--- and we'd like the 1D21-0310 in evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 1D75, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No further questions at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic. Mr. Dieckmann to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hansen. My name is Jens Dieckmann and I am I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Mr. Hansen, on the 28th and 29th October 2008, you met in The Hague with Mr. Groome from the Prosecution, true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And it was to conduct a proofing session, true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: In this proofing session, you stated, and I want to put it to you from the proofing note we received from the Prosecution, a quote: "Photos of Sredoje Lukic were never used in a photo identification procedure of concerns that they could not be made to appear neutral with other fill-in photographs and because the photographs were on the fugitive posters prominently displayed in the former Yugoslavia." As I understood your testimony today on page 12, line 16, of the provisional transcript, you stand by this statement today?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Hansen doesn't have the benefit of seeing whatever's on 12 -- whatever the transcript reference was that he is being asked whether he stands by that statement. If it could be read to him, perhaps he would be able -- in a better position to affirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let line 16 on page 12 be read to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: It's: "No. We decided not to show any photograph of Sredoje Lukic because of the quality of the -- it wasn't original tape but we will call it the original tape. It was very poor quality." May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
