utterances.text: Well, the witness is looking at it, so we'll wait for his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not what I said because I said I used the, quoting, "original tape," but it was a tape we got that we called the original tape, but it -- the actual tape was far from the original. It was a very poor -- I think it was third or fourth copy of something. It was a poor quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Is it true that you never used a photo of Sredoje Lukic in a photo identification procedure?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Ms. Court Usher, we could please show to the witness, 2D20. It is a witness statement tendered into evidence from 7th November 2000 of Mr. Adem Berberovic, former VG-03. Could we show it on the screen, please. Thank you. The English version. Yes, thank you. Could we go to the bottom of the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, is this your signature on the left side of the page?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And this confirms that you conducted the interview with Mr. Berberovic on the 7th November 2000?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Could we go now to page 3 of the English version of this witness statement to the bottom of the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, now, I would like to read to you the last paragraph of page 3: "You have showed me a photospread with 12 photo of men. Picture 3 is Sredoje Lukic. Picture 3 is Milan Lukic and 9 is Mitar Vasiljevic, but he looks older than I remember him and he has no mustache. I can tell you for sure that 11 is a man from Visegrad, I cannot remember his name."

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I think that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: You take then that you never used a photo of Sredoje Lukic in photo identification procedures, and that you conducted the interview with Adem Berberovic. Do you agree with me that picture 3 on this photospread shown to Mr. Berberovic was not Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Let me explain. I think this is a statement that, unfortunately, doesn't have a photospread attached. We couldn't find that photospread during the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: And I am quite --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Could you just -- I am sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: I put a question to you and I just invite you to answer my question. If you never used a photo of Sredoje Lukic, photo 3 could never be Sredoje Lukic; isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I'll agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. After the statement was produced, you gave the statement together with the photospread to the Prosecution, didn't you not?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Who was your contact person at the OTP in the year of 2000 you have given this statement and the photospread from Mr. Adem Berberovic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Returning from a mission to The Hague, the first task for the team was to, what we call, MFI or at the time IF the document electronically. So we updated something in the system and with a printout of the MFI front page we went to evidence unit with the actual statement, the attachment and the MFI front page, and then it was up to evidence unit to handle the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Another topic, sir. You worked as an investigator for the ICTY Prosecution from 1995 up to 2006 with a short period of interruption, as you explained to us; is it true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: When you first began work for the ICTY, you were trained in how to conduct investigations at the ICTY, true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't say exactly trained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Were there training courses to make you familiar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. Let him say what it was. He says it's not exactly trained, then what was it? Witness, how would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a person attached who told me about the system in the house and the way the investigations were done. It wasn't education, so it wasn't that way. It was learning by doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: You do not remember or --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's not because I don't want.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Okay. Was --

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. I can tell you in 1999, when I came, I was attached to Yves Roy, so we worked closely together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: This person was a Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, he was an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Have you been aware of the existence of the OTP identification guidelines for photographic procedures during your work as an investigator?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I might have seen it, but I don't remember when. Is it from the, I have to ask a question, is it from the Rules of Procedure and Evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: I came to this later on, sir. So, my learned friend Mr. Alarid showed to you a document on the screen; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: The OTP guidelines. When did you see this document the first time, could you remember?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: But you have seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: You believe so, does it mean you are not sure?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure because I can't answer that question before I'm told where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Sir, this document has been disclosed from the Prosecution to the Defence and this is the OTP guidelines for the work of the Prosecution investigation at the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Sir, let us go a moment back to the statement from the 7th November 2000 of Mr. Adem Berberovic. Do you agree with me that according to the statement on the third page, on the last paragraph regarding the photospread, that you did not ask Mr. Berberovic before you showed him the photospreads whether he had already seen the suspect in a photo, TV or a poster? You did not verify this point.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: According to the statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just meaning that you did not verify the point put to you by counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Ms. Court Usher, could we call up again 1D74, the OTP guidelines. And just go to the middle. I am sorry, to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And I would like to read to you the first sentence under the headline: "Procedure with witness." "The investigator must ascertain whether the witness has seen the suspect in a photograph, on television or a poster. It may be that the photoboard procedure would then be inappropriate." Do you agree with me that following the statement of Mr. Adem Berberovic, page 3, this conduct of photo identification with Mr. Berberovic was not in accordance to the OTP guidelines?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No. Because not everything that was discussed between the investigator and the witness was put on paper. Can I have a look at the bottom line of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Bottom line from this document?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No, no, the very bottom of the page. Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: But, sir, you agree with me that the statement of Mr. Adem Berberovic does not present any information about it that you have asked this question?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: The statement of Berberovic doesn't contain those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Ms. Court Usher, could we call the document with the ERN number 0642-8898. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: I refer to your prior testimony today on page 19, line 20, where you said that this photospread from the 17, 18 December 1998 was shown to VG-014, 24 and 25. This is your statement?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's according to the statement taken during those two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: So you used this photospread three times with these three witnesses?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I didn't use a photospread.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: But it was used by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It was used by somebody, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Could we go back to 1D74, please. And could we go to page 2, and the upper part of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, I would like to read out to you the third and fourth bullet point. "If it is intended to show photoboards to more than one witness on a mission, several photoboards should be prepared, if possible, with the photographs arranged in a different sequence in each photoboard. Each should then be photocopied." Next one: "Once you have a positive identification, ideally the photoboard should not be used with other witnesses. If this is necessary, however, the positions of the photographs should be changed and the suspect's photograph, in particular, should be moved. Take a fresh photocopy of the new layout for use in the procedure." Mr. Hansen, do you agree with me that the frequent use of the photospread from 17, 18 December 1998 for the witnesses 14, 24 and 25 is not in accordance with this part of the OTP guidelines?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: That's correct because there are no suspect on that photoboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tender -- I'm sorry. Your Honours, could we tender the photospread 0642-8898 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I'm not mistaken, isn't that in evidence as 1D75? Am I incorrect in that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: No. I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number 2D27, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Court Usher, could we go to ERN number 0206-2640.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: This is a photospread from 11th and up to 15th May 2000. Could we go to the next page. Thank you. Mr. Hansen, this signature are your signatures; is it true?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: No. It's Yves Roy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you. Are you in a position to identify if all the three signatures are the same signatures of Mr. Yves Roy?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This unreadable thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this practice of signing on the back side of a photospread an indication that this photospread was used exactly the four times with the signature here?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: It looks so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Could it be admitted into evidence under these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number 2D28, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to ERN number 0100-5961. Sorry, this is number 13 on the exhibit list of the Prosecution sent to us before this session. Number 13. Sorry, perhaps it's -- no. Yes, this is 0100-5961. Photospread from 12 and 13th June 2000. So we have a hard copy here, I don't know. So it will be shown? Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at this photospread, it was a photospread from the 12th and 13th June 2000 which was used with VG-119. This photospread is identical to the one used on the 11th May 2000 I showed you before, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Shall we show you the other one?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Can we put the other one next to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps is it possible to show the first page side by side from both documents? The other document was 0206-2640, tendered into evidence with 2D28. This is the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that both are identical?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Can we show the second page of both documents, if possible. The next one, the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: You agree with me that also the second page is identical?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And do you agree with me that this use of this photospreads, those documents, is also not in accordance with OTP guidelines for using photospreads, page 2, bullet points 3 and 4, I read out to you some minutes before?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: I need to know on which dates those photospreads were used. I think you mentioned the date but I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes, the first page was used in May 2000, 11th through the 15th of May, 2000. And the document on the right side was used on the 12th and 13th June 2000 with VG-119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What guidelines do you say they breach, Mr. Dieckmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: It is from the guidelines page 2 and the third and fourth bullet point I read out because the same photoboards are shown to more than one witness without any change, and even in the case they have been suspect in it. Yes. The third bullet point: "If it is intended to show photoboards to more than one witness on a mission, several photoboards should be prepared, if possible, with the photographs arranged in a different sequence in each photoboard. Each should then be photocopied." And here in fact it was shown to VG-058, the first document, and the other one was shown to VG-119 on the same mission, just one month after the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And they are the same? Are you saying they are the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: I say they contain the same photos and in the same arrangement, and they are identical, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The photos on the left you say are identical to those on the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will it be a matter of appreciation. Let's hear what the witness answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know much about this because one was shown by Yves Roy, the other one was shown by Finn Tollefson. The circumstances I don't know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tender the document 0100-5961 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the photospreads on --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: The right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the right side?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Admitted as Exhibit number 2D29, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Ms. Court Usher, could we go to ERN number 0206-2586. Thank you. Could we go on the second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree with me that there are signatures of four different persons with four different dates?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: On the left corner of the page it is VG-059. On the right side is VG-064. Then left on the left side down it is VG-063, and down on the right side is VG-13.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go into private session, Your Honours. And it should be redacted, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session. And a redaction.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: My question to you was: Was there a monetary reward advertised on this poster for capture of the people contained on it?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And can you give the Chamber some idea of the distribution of these posters, how widespread, how commonly were they available in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: If you know, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How is that speculation? Either he knows or he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd ask for a -- lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've seen quite many posters when they were distributed in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And where would these posters be posted?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: In official offices, post offices, banks, police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alarid brought out, this was the photospread that was shown to VG-032, one of the Drina survivors, can you tell us what that person said with respect to Mr. Lukic's photo on this photospread?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't have the benefit of this exhibit when the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He testified on direct to what he said. Mr. Groome is asking him to repeat himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Has this question already been asked because we don't want to be wasting time, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did not have a -- this was not on the 65 ter list so I did not, in fairness attempt, to use it. Now that it is a Defence exhibit, I would like to ask the witness what he recalls about what VG-032 said about it. I did ask him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the answer, Witness? What is the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The witness that I met outside former Yugoslavia picked Mitar Vasiljevic, number 1 in the top left corner, with 100 percent. And concerning Milan Lukic, he put his finger -- let me just -- he put his finger on the picture and said: "This is Milan Lukic, but I'm only 90 percent sure. That's why I don't want to sign the photo."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I now ask that the witness be shown 1D75. I believe I have the right exhibit. And could we go to the second page of this exhibit. Is there another page with a close-up of the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: You were asked on cross-examination whether VG-014, another survivor of the Drina River, was given an opportunity to see this. My question to you is: When this photograph was shown to that person, did he make any comment on the hair of the person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: Since I don't have the statement with me, I have to say I'm not quite sure but he said something about curly hair. I don't remember the quoting in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: And what did he say generally with respect to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He just answered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let him finish his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He just said without the benefit of the statement he can't be sure, so he is being asked to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear the question. What is the question you are asking, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask him --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall what he said in comparing this person to the person that he was telling you was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: IB JUL HANSEN
utterances.text: He said this person was curly -- had curly hair where Milan Lukic didn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: May I have recross, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Re-cross, yes. Based on the questioning of the -- because I have the statement so we can put that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe -- I think the only time re-cross is appropriate is if I've gone outside the boundaries of cross-examination and I haven't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that procedure. We don't have that here --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, he -- and he has gone outside the bounds of cross-examination. I didn't talk about the statement and -- or nor asked this witness to refer or recollect the statement and we have the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't introduce this exhibit. It was introduced by Mr. Alarid, he asked questions about. I simply asked a questions arising out of his use of this exhibit. There's no grounds here for a renewed -- if Mr. Alarid wants to make an application to re-open his cross-examination, that's one thing, but it certainly isn't a matter for re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see where the re-examination did not arise from cross-examination, Mr. Alarid. So I don't understand how you would have any basis for asking permission to ask further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we tender, then, the statement simply into evidence? It is a statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's 1D21 -- excuse me, we have the ERN number. 00672114 and 200672115.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I must say I'm concerned that the VG-014 has been here, has testified. If there's something in his statement that Mr. Alarid wanted to put it him, it seem that that would have been the appropriate time. I'm not even sure whether Mr. Hansen is the investigator who actually took the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. MR. ALARID, and Your Honour, the problem is -- that regards to that is the photos that Mr. Groome said he just found, we didn't have, so we didn't have the ability to cross-examine that witness with the photos. We've introduced the photos, so I think the statement relating to the photos should come in accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will concede that that is correct, that those photos were found recently after VG-014 had completed his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, what can this witness say about the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You just allowed him to testify as to what occurred during that statement which he didn't take, so I think the best evidence is the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number 1D76, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution now calls Amor Masovic. Mr. Adam Weber will be doing the examination of Mr. Amor Masovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before the witness is called, we received today a motion filed by the Defence for Milan Lukic to bar the Prosecution from the introduction into evidence of the proffered Exhibit statement of Amor Masovic and related testimony. First, I'd like to ask Defence why is this motion so late? Mr. Masovic is testifying today. MR.IVETIC: Is that a serious question, Your Honour? With the manner in which the Prosecution have been filing motions and the fact that we've been responding to them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't you ask me if it's a serious question. That's out of order. MR.IVETIC: I -- I apologise, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If I ask you the question, you answer it. MR.IVETIC: Your Honour, it was filed late because we -- as Your Honour knows, the Prosecution provided information yesterday. We were going to file the motion last night, but I had to review the documentation that the Prosecution had just disclosed to us for this witness in order to make sure that there was not anything further that needed to be included in the motion with respect to objections asked to Mr. Masovic. We have been responding to the Prosecution's case, witness by witness. Your Honour knows I've been assigned as co-counsel on this case rather recently. The original 65 ter summary for Mr. Masovic does not include any of the factors that are raised in the witness statements for which we are objecting to. The original mode of testimony was set to be -- was set to be viva voce in the latest in the latest witness notification for this witness. Yesterday was the first time that they indicated he would be brought 92 ter and that the statement, which had been listed just as an exhibit that might be referred to, now becomes actual as being the bulk of his testimony. And I apologise again, in the heat of the moment, to making the comments to Your Honour as I -- as I -- reflecting back, some of these matters may not be part of the public record and therefore may not be available to Your Honour. And again I apologise and take back the comments I made at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Part of the difficulty, of course, is that we have to rule, we have to hear arguments on this motion. It's a motion to bar the testimony of the witness who is to testify now. MR.IVETIC: One suggestion I have on that, Your Honour, one thing we did do in another case, the case wherein the decision is cited from Milutinovic et al. We heard the witness, kept the motion pending, and then following the completion of the testimony of the witness, having the full picture of the witness's qualifications, testimony, et cetera, the Trial Chamber then made its ruling. And that was something -- that's why I asked for oral submissions, that was something I was going to propose in this instance. Given the fact that we have Mr. Masovic here, we have time in the courtroom, which is quite valuable, and that was what I was going to suggest to Your Honours as a viable alternative. Just so long as you do realize that it is a very serious motion that has -- and I've taken the effort to give everything to Your Honours in the written motion so that you have the full picture that you need to reach your decision. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What should we then -- should we follow that procedure and at the end of the day agree with the motion, we would have our wasted time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. At 1.24 p.m. today, the Prosecution received an e-mail containing a courtesy copy of Milan Lukic motion to -- seeking to bar the Prosecution from the introduction into evidence of the proffered exhibit statement of Amor Masovic, which is referenced as the statement of the 4th of September, 2008, and related testimony. The relevant procedural history relating to Mr. Masovic is as follows: On the 15 of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you are going too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Of course. On the 15th of February, 2008, the Prosecution filed a motion to admit the testimony and related exhibits of Amor Masovic pursuant to Rule 92 bis. This is over 8 months ago. After being granted an extension during a status conference on the 12th of March, 2008, the accused filed his response to the Prosecution's 92 bis submission for Mr. Masovic. In this response, the accused requested the ability to cross-examine the witness but did not raise any issues pursuant to Rule 94 bis. On the 22nd of August, 2008, the Trial Chamber issued its decision allowing Mr. Masovic pursuant to Rule 92 bis to appear before this Tribunal with the Prosecution to lay the foundation for Mr. Masovic's exhibits pursuant to Rule 92 ter and for cross-examination. No motion for certification of appeal was filed on behalf of either of the accused in relation to this decision. On the 22nd of September, 2008, the Prosecution filed its motion to add an updated statement of Amor Masovic dated the 4th of September, 2008, this included updated tables and a B/C/S version of the witness's curriculum vitae. The Prosecution disclosed the English translation of the curriculum vitae on the 26th of September, 2008, over a month ago. On the 7th of October, the accused response -- filed a response to that motion. This response, again, did not raise any of the substantive issues that are raised in the current filing made today. This was the proper forum to raise these concerns in relation to the witness's statement of the 4th of September, 2008, which the Defence now claims to be making today. But this two-page motion that was filed in response on the 7th of October did not contain any of these matters. There was no response filed on behalf of the co-accused, Sredoje Lukic. On the 23rd of October, 2008, the Chamber issued its decision admitting the updated statement and tables of Mr. Masovic. This updated statement is what is the subject of the current motion that's pending today. It was in the context of this litigation, over the course of 8 months, that the matter of whether the substance of Mr. Masovic's evidence falls rightly under 94 bis or under 92 bis should have been rightly raised by the Defence. They had adequate opportunity to do so. The proper forum for this discussion would have been in the response to the Prosecution's motion to admit the testimony of Mr. Masovic under 92 bis filed on the 15th of February.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, please, for the benefit of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would have been to raise these issues in the response to the Prosecution's motion to admit the testimony of Mr. Masovic under 92 bis filed on the 15th of February, 2008, or alternatively, in the response to the motion to admit the updated statement and tables filed on the 22nd September 2008. There are rules of procedure which we are all required to follow with respect to the timeliness of submissions before this Tribunal. These submissions -- this submission that is filed today is not timely and thus not abiding by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The Defence's wish is have an unhindered right to raise any matter at any time in any format. This should not be permitted. Based on these reasons, the Prosecution requests that the Trial Chamber bar this motion from being filed and proceed with Mr. Masovic's testimony in full today pursuant to the previous rulings of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You say it should have been filed when? Just remind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The accused had multiple opportunities to raise this issue. We filed a motion to admit Mr. Masovic's materials in the Vasiljevic case and related exhibits back on the 15th of February, 2008. They filed a response to that in March of 2008, March 28th. We then filed an additional -- well, just going back. There was a decision on that submission rendered by the Tribunal -- rendered by the Chamber on the 22nd of August, 2008. They could have raised that in a certification to appeal that decision; they failed to do so. Then we submitted an additional updated statement on the 22nd of September, 2008, in which they could have raised these issues in response. On the 7th of October, 2008, they failed to raise those issues in the response, and those would have been the opportunities that they would have had to raise these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, Mr. Alarid then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The only thing that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. Just -- I'm not asking you about that. Forget for the moment the question of the timeliness of the motion. What is the substantive issue that it raises? MR.IVETIC: Twofold, Your Honour. The witness statement of Amor Masovic, which I presume is going to be the bulk of his testimony, has two deficiencies. First of all, we did not know the expert nature of his testimony until his new report was received in September. The statement purports to indicate -- and we did object to the report. The statement indicates that he is reaching conclusions and making an analysis of certain data that is in the possession of his organisation and certain statements of out-of-court declarants. The thrust of our motion, Your Honour, is that for the past two days, at least twice this Trial Chamber has prevented Defence counsel from using statements of out-of-court declarants with the witness who is not the out-of-court declarant. Mr. Masovic is -- almost the entirety of his testimony in the statement is doing exactly that which the Defence was denied the ability to do. So I would dictate, irrespective of the filing issue, the interests of justice, equality of arms and having a fair and impartial proceeding dictate that this matter be addressed. And indeed I did not have to file a motion, I could have objected at the time that the witness is called when they seek to introduce an exhibit, which is what we'd intended to do when he was listed as a live witness. But in any event, the second thrust of that, and I've cited to the decision in the Milutinovic case where the Trial Chamber, chaired by the Honourable Judge Bonomy, did in fact bar, after hearing the testimony, those statements saying, this is page 10 of the decision: "Most of the tendered excerpts of the challenged reports set forth allegations of criminal conduct made by persons who claim to be victims or witnesses to these crimes. Not having had the opportunity of a hearing, any of the persons upon whose statements these excerpts are based, the Chamber is not in a position to assess the reliability of the factual contentions contained therein. So we object to the portion of Mr. Masovic's statement that is the result of his review of an untold number, unidentified and undisclosed by the Prosecution, witness statements collected by the Bosnian authorities upon which -- which he is now retelling to this Trial Chamber in his report. Secondly, on the issue of being an expert, the CV and other material that has been disclosed does not make him an expert. There has been no filing by Prosecution seeking to submit him as an expert, and therefore, the portions of statement that purport to give expert opinions are therefore improper. And I've said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is he being called as an expert? MR.IVETIC: I don't know to this day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not my understanding, that he is being called as an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, reading this statement that they even call a report sounds like it's an expert to me. I think they are trying to sneak in pseudo-expert testimony through a factual witness. I would like to submit if they stick to what was in the 65 ter summary, that the witness, a lawyer by profession, was the president of the state commission, and if he will talk about the operation of the commission, his attendance at exhumations, the locations of exhumations, the number of human remains that were recovered, that all is unobjectionable. And if that is what he is testifying about, I have no objection and I have no cross-examination. But all this new material since the 65 ter was filed in March of 2008, changes the picture dramatically, and in light of the cases that I've cited, I believe is a matter that needs to be considered and which affects the integrity of this evidence that's being offered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of the motion, we have a reference at(b) to: "Our team searched the ruins of those houses on several occasions, but until today, we have not located remains of the victims. And it leads to the conclusion that mortal remains were moved to secondary locations." Now "conclusion" is in bold. What is the point you want to make about that? MR.IVETIC: If Your Honour reads further in the motion, you'll see that we have delineated in there, trying to differentiate between the portion of that that is acceptable testimony, i.e., that they went to the site, they performed examination, no mortal remains were found. But where he says the conclusion you draw from that is that there were remains and they were removed, that is the providence of the Trial Chamber to make that legal conclusion based upon the forensic or factual evidence that is presented. This lawyer by profession who is a Prosecution witness is not in a position to present that as evidence that this Trial Chamber is then bound by to consider the charges in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Wouldn't the proper course then be for you -- wouldn't the proper then course be for you in cross-examination to examine him as to his qualifications to make that conclusion and thereby demonstrate that the conclusion is worthless? And ask us to disregard it. MR.IVETIC: With respect to that, Your Honour, that is absolutely correct and with respect to that I can cross-examine him. Where I can't cross-examine him is why he says, I've read statements and based upon these statements I conclude that this event happened. I don't know the statements that he reviewed. I don't have access to them and I don't know how many there are, how they were taken, who they are from. That is the part that I cannot successfully and properly confront him and cross-examine him on. So I agree, there are portions of this that I could examine him on. Therefore, I think that he -- you know, hearing him, there's parts of his testimony that is proper, so he will be heard in some form or another, I believe, no matter how the Trial Chamber rules. That's why I think that we should at least have an opportunity to look at the stuff that is beyond what would be proper testimony for him in our submission and see which of that comes in, which of it doesn't, because if we are talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Remind me again of the decision in the Milutinovic case. MR.IVETIC: The decision in the Milutinovic case -- THE COURT: You referred to it in your motion? MR.IVETIC: Yes, Your Honour. It's footnoted. I have a copy here that I have only highlighted one page on and written on the first page. I can take the first page off. It's the 1st September 2006 decision on evidence tendered through Sandra Mitchell and Frederick Abrahams. Those were the -- Your Honour, and I know you probably remember from the Milosevic case, those were the as seen, as told, and under-orders books that were presented in both proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But wasn't that -- in that case wasn't the witness an expert? Wasn't he -- he wasn't tendered as an expert? MR.IVETIC: No, Your Honour. They're tendered as a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters. Thank you very much. MR.IVETIC: -- question were tendered as exhibits by the Prosecution to be used in the live testimony of those witnesses, or I take that back, they were 92 ter witnesses, though.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the record, please. Thank you. Slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, is it paragraph 10 that you are referring to? Because I see in paragraph 12 a reference to Milutinovic and a reference to Philip Coo. Is that the -- MR.IVETIC: I believe so. There should be -- there should be one -- one was an oral decision and one was a written decision. In the footnote they should have 1 September 2006 decision, that would be the written decision of some 15 or 20 pages, I think it is. And the other one was the oral ruling for which I gave the transcript reference. I unfortunately don't have the copy of my motion in front of me. It's footnotes 2 and 5 of our motion, Your Honour. I apologise again for not having a copy in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The difficulty that the Chamber faces is that we now have to assess this motion very quickly and give a decision on it. So the question of timeliness is in fact quite relevant. But I would not be minded, I would not be disposed to dismiss it on that ground. My background doesn't allow me to do that. I like to look at the substance of things. So I would be prepared to apply Rule 127, even if I did find it was out of time, and not bar it on that ground. And let's get to the substance and deal with the substance. Now, let me hear you, Mr. Weber, on the substantive points very quickly, and then I think I'll have to adjourn briefly to consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As Your Honour noted, timing is an issue. This just came to the Prosecution's attention this afternoon, less than an hour before court was to begin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you can't really plead that now. I mean the substantive questions are -- I mean, this is part of our case law.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in terms of Mr. Masovic, he is the president of the Bureau of the Institute for Missing Persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the past -- in the period of time between 1995 and 2008, the witness took part in the search, exhumations, autopsies, and identification procedures of more than 17.000 victims exhumed from 370 mass graves and more than 3800 individual grave sites. During the course of these investigations, of course he had conversations with other individuals. These are what we refer to as statements in his report. Contrary to what has been asserted, the report does not indicate that these are some form of written statements from other people. My belief is that Mr. Masovic had conversations with other people and thus acquired knowledge during his very extensive experience. In terms of the case that's referenced by counsel in support of his position, I believe in that matter, there were summaries of eyewitness testimonies in that expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to alert my legal officers to get a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, I do not have a copy of the case with me right now. But that would be a very different circumstance than what we are dealing with in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In what way do you say it's different?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, the portions that were not admissible, with respect to that expert in that case, was the fact that there were statements from eyewitnesss. Mr. Masovic has been admitted pursuant to 92 bis because his statements do not reference the acts and conduct of the accused. These references in his current statement do not reference things that relate to eyewitness testimony or eyewitness descriptions of the conduct of either Milan or Sredoje Lukic. Therefore, it's distinguishable from the decision which is being offered in support here, and this witness should be allowed to testify here today and this report should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, under the circumstances might I just add a short comment. It seems from what Mr. Ivetic has said is he doesn't object to some of what Mr. Masovic is going to testify to, so can I make the suggestion that we proceed with that portion and whatever portion of Mr. Masovic's testimony Mr. Ivetic takes objection to and believes is the substance of this motion, could he flag it to the Chamber and then could we have an opportunity to look at these cases. And I agree with Your Honour that we shouldn't just dismiss a substantive issue because of timing, but it is important the Prosecution have a fair opportunity to look at the issue and study the cases and have a -- be able to give an informed view to the Chamber. So what I'm suggesting is that we do proceed at least on the portion that is in agreement as perfectly proper, and if Mr. Ivetic flags those portions of the testimony which he feels are the subject of this motion, then we could make some progress today and the Prosecution would have an opportunity, although we are working on several motions and submissions for the Chamber, we would try to, as expeditiously as possible, present our view on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a pragmatic approach. The question is -- sorry, I'm saying that's pragmatic approach, but the question is how soon will -- in the examination-in-chief will these issues arise? Can you steer clear of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Pursuant to the Chamber's decision on the 22nd of August, 2008, the Prosecution was going to only lay the 92 ter foundation for the prior Vasiljevic testimony and exhibits and then subsequently the report and attached exhibits and then tender the witness for cross-examination. There's going to be no direct questions elicited.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, I apologise, Your Honour, for up and down but then it seems to me that then we could deal with -- Mr. Ivetic could simply point to which portions of that should be struck depending upon the Chamber's decision in this matter. And that's something that could be done after the witness is taken here today

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the break now, so we'll take the break. The break would be half an hour unless you are notified otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you referred to a Trial Chamber which, when faced with this kind of decision, heard the evidence first and then decided on the question of admissibility after. What case was that? MR.IVETIC: That is the Milutinovic. That's the decision that was cited, that was what -- how that occurred, procedurally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have the decision here. It's all of 18 pages. I believe you -- in the interest of judicial economy, I'm disposed to find favour with Mr. Ivetic's approach, which is that we hear the evidence first and then decide on the question of admissibility thereafter. The issues raised by the motion are serious issues. They are substantive legal issues. The position would then be afforded an opportunity to present any arguments that it wishes in relation to the motion, but I believe this is the best course to adopt in the circumstances, so we'll hear the evidence. We are trying to finish this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will try to get a response as soon as possible, but noting that the standard period for response would exceed the time that the Prosecution intends to rest, we may be asking the Chamber to rest conditionally pending our response, but we will try to get our response in before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Under Rule 127 we can vary the time, either up or down. Up or down. And that is what we will do in order to achieve the most expeditious result. So let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There was one matter raised prior to the witness commencing testimony. This past prior Monday, the Chamber asked for a copy of Mr. Masovic's curriculum vitae in English. I don't know if the Chamber is in a position to render a decision today as to whether or not that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The CV will be admitted subject to the procedures under 92 ter being complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Amor Masovic. By profession I'm a lawyer. At present I am performing the duty of a member of the federal parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, I'm an MP, and the president of the Bureau for Justice, member of the Commission for the Protection of Human Rights, and a member of the Constitutional Commission in the parliament of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And at present, I'm occupying the post of president of the Collegium of Directors or Bureau of the Institute for Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Masovic, did you testify in the case of Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic on the dates of the 24th and 25th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review that testimony in the Bosnian language before coming to court here today?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions here today, would you provide the same answers as you provided during the course of your Vasiljevic testimony?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: To the general questions I would give the same answers. With respect to the questions that specifically related to certain names and surnames of missing persons, identified persons, numbers and figures from my testimony, then my answers today would be somewhat different because seven years have elapsed since then and the trial, and the search for missing persons and the exhumation of victims from graves and identification of victims as well has progressed considerably during that period of time, that is to say, since the time I testified in the Vasiljevic trial to the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, the Prosecution tenders into evidence Amor Masovic's previous testimony in the Vasiljevic case which are 65 ter numbers 50 and 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter number 50 will become Exhibit P172, and 65 ter number 51 will become Exhibit number P173.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders the underlying exhibits which were authenticated during the course of the Vasiljevic testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may have just one clarification related to other exhibits from that testimony. Do we admit now just -- is it admitted now just the transcript without other exhibits or admission of other exhibits is automatically with the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution didn't even finish its question. We just so far offered 65 ter number 50 and 51, which was the previous testimony, the transcripts. During the course of that testimony, there were a number of exhibits admitted, specifically nine. Based on that previous testimony we were then going to tender now the nine exhibits that were authenticated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Right. Yes, we'll admit those.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, that's 65 ter numbers 41 through 49. Nine exhibits in total.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 41 is now Exhibit P174. 42 is Exhibit P175. 43 is Exhibit P176. 44 is Exhibit P177. 45 is Exhibit P178. 46 is Exhibit P179. 47 is Exhibit P180. 48 is Exhibit P181. And 49 is Exhibit P182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now is okay. Thank you, Your Honour, for this opportunity. Could those exhibits -- could they be marked for identification because as far as I understood the decision, the final decision will be after the testimony of this witness, about all the exhibits and complete testimony? Maybe I have wrong understanding of the previous order, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's really a question of what is the most practicable procedure. I don't see any harm in the decision that we have taken because if subsequently we decide to -- that the evidence is not admissible, then all of that would be disregarded. But let me hear Mr. Weber on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In terms of whether or not these exhibits should be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Groome, what do you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I agree with Your Honour that it really makes no difference. I mean the Chamber can either admit them later or remove them from the Exhibit list. So my suggestion would be to leave them as they are now and if the Chamber in its written decision could deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll just leave them as they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Masovic, did you have an occasion to provide an updated statement concerning the commission's work and your personal work to the ICTY which was dated the 4th of September, 2008?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review that statement in the Bosnian language prior to your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If the OTP request admission of this statement, I oppose. Because this statement is not taken in a proper form as other OTP statements are. This is completely something different. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's wait and see. Let's wait and see what he does with it. Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For clarification, this is a statement that you personally provided and then sent to the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this a statement that was taken in the presence of an ICTY Office of the Prosecutor investigator?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I compiled the statement after talking to the investigators of the Tribunal, and then I sent it to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today, which were your statements in the September 4th, 2008 statement, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is the statement that you provided true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: The statement partially incorporates statistical data which were taken over from the database that the institute has at its disposal, the Institute for Missing Persons of which I'm the head, one of the members of the bureau or, rather, the president, and in the portion in which that statement does not have to do with statistical data, my statement would be exactly the same today as it was last time. So I stand behind the statement wholly, the one that I sent to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders the statement of Amor Masovic, dated the 4th of September, 2008, into evidence. It is ERN number 06412173 through 06412181, and the corresponding English translation is under ERN ET-06412173 through 06412181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And this is 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Pursuant to the Chamber's decision of 23rd of October, 2008, this statement is being admitted pursuant to 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you had a point? And Mr. Ivetic as well, but Mr. Cepic first.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could I give the turn to Mr. Ivetic just to find decision, please, Your Honour, if I have that 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, yes. MR.IVETIC: Your Honours, I can be very brief in this. As I'm reading the witness's response, it seems to he is disavowing the statistical portion and limiting his answer to the part that is not the statistical portion, that that is the part that he would adopt and that it is accurate. So given the record as it is now on the transcript, I'm not sure that the formalities of Rule 92 ter have been achieved as to the entire statement which might short circuit my cross-examination if in fact that portion is out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, how do you answer that, that -- the contention that the witness has disavowed the statistical portion of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't believe necessarily the witness has disavowed it. If the Chamber would like, I'd be happy to ask additional questions to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Masovic, you just provided an answer in which you made reference to both the statistical portions of your 4th of September, 2008, statement separate from the remainder of your statement. Could you explain -- please explain the answer that you provided in reference to your statistical portions of your statement and whether or not those portions would be different today.

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood the question, but I'll do my best to answer it as I did understand it. My statement of the 4th of September represents a sort of updating of data provided during the testimony in the Vasiljevic trial. So some of the data, especially the tables and the annexes that go along with my statement have been updated. They are an update of the information data and tables that I presented during my written and oral testimony in the Vasiljevic trial. This present statement contains additions in comparison to the Vasiljevic testimony with respect to comparisons made in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the statistical data about the missing women and children, the number of missing women and children, and the number of missing persons, elderly persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand what you are saying. You had a point, Mr. Cepic, what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, completely frankly, I never seen in my practice -- in a previous practice that the OTP requested admission of the statement, of OTP witness statement which hasn't got any signature of OTP investigator or someone else. I just see here the signature of Mr. Masovic at the last page, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can it be shown on the e-court so that I can see it. Your point is that there's no signature of the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The investigator who took the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The investigator did not take the statement. Mr. Masovic provided it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Masovic provided it. So that's the answer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit the statement under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P183, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders the attached exhibits to that statement which are located under ERN 0641-2271 through 0641-2333. These are the updated statements and charts that were provided with the 4th of September, 2008, statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, as I can see, all those documents which my learned friend now quoted are not assigned yet, on 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are not?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Not yet assigned. I can give this --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Chamber on the 23rd of October, 2008, admitted these exhibits. The Prosecution, I believe as Mr. Cepic is referring to, we haven't assigned 65 ter numbers to it, but the Chamber has allowed these documents it its previous decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Pursuant to today's decision relating to the curriculum vitae, the Prosecution now tenders Mr. Masovic's curriculum vitae into evidence. It's 65 ter numbers 06412268 through 06412270, along with the corresponding English translation under the same ERN dash ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit the CV.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P185, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks. Then Mr. Ivetic. MR.IVETIC: Thank you, Your Honours. And again I apologise for being so abrupt previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Masovic, my name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys for Mr. Milan Lukic today. First of all, I'd like to focus on the report that is number P183 -- or, excuse me, the witness statement P183 and your sections 7 through 10, that is what I think you referred to as your statistical analysis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the interpreter is asking you to slow down. MR.IVETIC: I should also probably switch channels so I can hear their warnings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Masovic, could you tell us, since your curriculum vitae is absent -- silent on this issue, whether you have any degrees in statistical analysis.

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I said in my introduction that I was a lawyer by profession and have some duties in the parliament today and the Institute for Missing Persons. I'm a graduate of law and I have passed the judiciary examination. I don't have any academic knowledge in the sphere of statistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Has -- thank you, sir. That is the statistical analysis portion of your statement been subjected to peer review by any statistical analysis academics and professionals, and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, it has not been subjected to scientific analysis it is purely on the bases of figures and data in the database and a comparative analysis, if you are referring to the last page of my statement, as I say, a comparative analysis which had as its goal to show the differences in the Visegrad municipality with respect to the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So there are analyses with respect to the number of missing persons, especially focusing on children and females who went missing from 1992 to 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What statistical sampling method was employed by you in the preparation of this aspect of your witness statement or report?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I compared the total number of missing persons in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the total number of missing persons, Bosniaks and Croats, in the Visegrad municipality. And then I applied that and looked at females and persons from 0 to 16 years of age, and also focused on the individuals who were over the age of 70 in order to show the difference in the data with respect to the Visegrad municipality. And in my conclusion, I put forward an observation of mine to the effect that the number of missing females significantly surpasses the overall number of missing women in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is to say, in Visegrad, there are three times as many women who are listed missing than there are in the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In percentages, not the absolute figure but percentage-wise. And then I also conducted an analysis of children up to the age of 18 and persons over the age of 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, as I'm sure you are aware, your statement has now been tendered to the Trial Chamber so we do have all of your analysis. I'm asking you about the methodology employed in reaching the same. What statistical controls did you use to flush out and harmonize variables that were present in the various municipalities that you reviewed in order to reach the conclusions you've reached in your report?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I have no pretensions in the sense that my report is a statistical report of any kind. It is a pure observation on the basis of my studies, that is to say, an analysis of the number of missing persons in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina compared to the number of missing persons in Visegrad municipality. And I said -- I explained to you how I came by those figures, comparing the total number of missing females with respect and in comparison to Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole. So no statistical method, that's my answer. No scientific statistic method was used in doing that and I have no pretensions in showing my report to be any kind of statistical report based on statistical research.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, how long do you intend to be? MR.IVETIC: I was hoping to finish today. I have about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I want to finish the witness today. Are you going to cross-examine, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long are you going to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer will you be? MR.IVETIC: At least 20 minutes if half an hour, depending on witness's answers. I've been trying to short-circuit through these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So we're close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's see how we get on then. Yes. MR.IVETIC:

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with that in mind, if we could try to keep the answers directed -- pointed to the question since we do have your report. Now, with respect to the findings in your statement, would it be accurate to say that they are based upon the information that you obtained from witness statements that in addition to your eyewitness of exhumations and also interviews of persons and also official documents of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it accurate to state that the rest of your report, apart from the statistical aspect, is based upon your review of statements taken by Bosnian agencies from witnesses, your own interviews with witnesses and families, and official documents of the Bosnian government in addition to your eyewitness of exhumation procedures?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, all of the above, and of course the records that the commissions have, commissions for exhumation which is the substantive part of my report. I'm talking about the tables which are exclusively based on official records kept with respect to missing persons. And I also used everything else that you enumerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Do you have any number of estimation as to the exact number of witness statements or interviews that you incorporated and whether they were all under oath to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: The records that you are referring to, which is the annexes to my report, are not the result of taking witness statements, but taking the information from the official records of missing and unidentified persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look at your report then. I guess we are going to have to do it this way. Page 4 of your report, I'm not talking about the annexure, page 4 of your report in the fourth paragraph states that: "Several dozen victims, according to statements of survivors, were executed and burnt at two locations in the town of Visegrad itself." How many statements did you review to reach this conclusion and were those statements all statements that were taken under oath to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: We do not take statements. That's not our job. We don't take statements under oath either. Perhaps I should explain at this point what the aim of the institute is and its existence. It is our task to locate individual, joint, and mass graves and to sound them out once we've established that they are graves, and then to inform the Prosecutor who then unleashes the process of exhumation and autopsies. So we are not a police organ, nor do we take any kinds of statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. The question was in the part of your report which reads: "Several dozen victims, according to the statements, were executed and burnt at two locations in the town of Visegrad itself." It's in your report so the question that is being asked is: How were those statements taken? Can you explain to us because it's in your report, so he is entitled to ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. So these are statements or interviews that we conducted with the surviving members of the families of these people. These were persons who came to the Commission for Missing Persons and they filed a request to have the relative struck down. In these two cases, I also had statements that were available to me. I'm not sure we are in open session, whether I am allowed to refer to specific names, perhaps they are witnesses in this trial, perhaps they are protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you can continue now. MR.IVETIC:

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Without going into names, you had mentioned some statements. How many statements did you review to reach your conclusion that is specified in here as to Pionirska and Bikavac and the houses that allegedly were burnt and the alleged grave sites containing dozens of victims resulting from these incidents?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: The houses were burned down, I have direct knowledge of this. One of these houses is no longer there, and the other has been -- or had been ruined to a large extent. The one on Pionirska Street, but again, we don't take the written affidavits from these family members. It is rather them who submit requests for their missing relatives to be found. Pursuant to that request, they state the personal details of these persons, the date of their disappearance, the place of their disappearance, the circumstances of these disappearance. What we do is this: We then take these names and we enter the names into our database of missing persons. It is then based on such evidence or such records, and these records exist and they are in our institute, I establish, for example, that a minimum of 46 persons from the Kurspahic family can be considered missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can short circuit this. Sir, is the crux of your testimony and is the only thing that you can actually affirmatively state that you are able to verify the names and numbers of people who are missing and not the manner in which they either met their demise or were missing? Is that what you are telling me, sir? Is that the limit of your capabilities in this report to give us just the verification of the names and numbers of people who are missing from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure if you've been following me. I'm telling you that family members, while talking to us, give us also the circumstances under which a person went missing. For example, once victims were chucked into the Drina River and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You are a lawyer, and now you are a witness. Can you differentiate between what is your testimony and what is the testimony of others that you are presenting? With respect to your testimony, is it limited to a verification of the identities and numbers of persons that are missing from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: AMOR MASOVIC
utterances.text: So, everything that you can find in this statement is based on existing evidence deriving from the records in the possession of the Institute for Missing Persons. I'm not testifying about this. I just got this from the existing records and the records suggest that certain persons went missing on a certain date at a certain place under a certain set of circumstances. I'm not testifying about that, I'm conveying the substance were our records.
